# Recreation Prompt

Create `Neon Loop Rush`, a browser-native mobile portrait endless runner. Preserve the mechanic truth of the source: a fixed-left circular player jumps only when grounded, gravity pulls it down, the world scrolls right-to-left, speed gradually increases, ring pickups add one score point, distance rises over time, and any hazard collision ends the run with a restart overlay.

Reframe the presentation as a Sonic-inspired high-speed neon loopway. The player is a blue quill speed rebel with a glowing trail and spin state. Rings are golden arcade loops. Hazards are red shock spikes and cyan-magenta breaker blocks. The background is a procedural night city speedway with checker rails, parallax loop arcs, star streaks, and speed lanes. Use short mobile-readable HUD vocabulary: Rings, Meters, Boost, Ring streak, Run wiped. Keep all code in a single inline `index.html` using Canvas, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Truth
The preserved source is a mobile-friendly canvas endless runner. A circular runner sits at a fixed x-position, falls under gravity, can jump only while grounded, scrolls through incoming hazards and ring groups, gains distance continuously, gains one score point per ring, and loses immediately on hazard collision. Start, game over, and restart are simple overlay states.

## Protected Mechanics
- One-button input: tap/click/Space/ArrowUp starts or jumps.
- Grounded-only jump with `gravity = 0.8`, `jumpForce = -15`, and player radius `20`.
- Horizontal world scrolling with speed starting at `8` and increasing by `0.002` per frame.
- Spawn cadence using the same random obstacle/ring choice and same obstacle/ring sizes.
- Collision semantics: circle player versus block rectangle, spike broad gate plus distance check.
- Ring score, distance display, immediate fail state, and restart reset.

## Remix Trajectory
The new surface reinterprets the same runner as a Sonic-like neon speed mastery game: a blue speed rebel dashes through loopway rails, collects rings, dodges breaker blocks and shock spikes, and survives an arcade city rush. The implementation remains a single inline Canvas/JS `index.html` for stability.
